title: The Thorp shuffle mixes in O(log n) steps
credit: Thorp (1973); problem popularised by Aldous-Diaconis and Morris; bounds by Morris, Montenegro-Tetali, Jiang
premise_risks: The best upper bound d^{5/3} is an unrefereed Oct 2026 preprint (arXiv 2610.18884); the refereed state of the art is O(d^3) (Morris 2013). The open target O(d) does not depend on it.
The 1/4 threshold is conventional; any fixed epsilon in (0,1) gives an equivalent statement up to constants by submultiplicativity.
plain: Take a deck of n = 2^d cards and cut it into two equal halves. For each i, the i-th card of each half are placed next to each other, with a fair coin deciding which goes on top. Repeat. A counting argument shows about 2d shuffles are needed before the deck can be close to uniformly random. Prove that a constant times d shuffles always suffice.
math: Let $n=2^d$, $h=n/2$. For $\xi\in\{0,1\}^h$ let $\sigma_\xi\in S_n$ put the cards from positions $i$ and $i+h$ into positions $2i,2i+1$, in that order if $\xi_i=0$ and swapped if $\xi_i=1$ ($0\le i<h$). Let $\mu_d$ be uniform on $\{\sigma_\xi\}$ and $t_{\rm mix}(d)=\min\{t:\|\mu_d^{*t}-U_{S_n}\|_{TV}\le 1/4\}$. Prove there is an absolute constant $C$ with $t_{\rm mix}(d)\le Cd$ for all $d\ge1$. (Counting the support gives $t_{\rm mix}(d)\ge(2-o(1))d$.)
review_note: Known: Lower bound $(2-o(1))d$ from counting (support of $\mu_d^{*t}$ has size at most $2^{tn/2}$). Upper bounds for $n=2^d$: $O(d^{44})$ (Morris 2005, AoP 2008), $O(d^{29})$ (Montenegro-Tetali), $O(d^4)$ (Morris, AoP 37 (2009), arXiv 0802.0339), $O(d^3)$ (Morris, Combin. Probab. Comput. 2013, arXiv 0912.2759), and $C_* d^{5/3}+O(d^{4/3}\log d)$ with $C_*\approx5.15$ (Y. Jiang, arXiv 2610.18884, Oct 2026, unrefereed). No O(d) or $d^{1+o(1)}$ bound is known.
